$molecule¶

Charge, multiplicity, geometry (Cartesian and/or Z-matrix) and per-atom basis sets.

Unlike the other groups, $molecule holds ordered data. It starts with the optional charge= and mult= (defaults 0 and 1), then one of the keywords cartesian or z-matrix, followed by one line per atom.

Cartesian lines: Z x y z. Z is the atomic number written as an integer: 8, not 8.0 and not O. The atom lines are read as a stream of numbers, so a value such as 8.0 shifts everything after it. In version 25 this gives no error: the run continues with a wrong molecule (extra atoms with Z=0) and a meaningless energy. Check the formula: and atom-count lines at the top of the output. The coordinates are in Å unless unit=b is given.

Z-matrix lines give the atomic number Z_i of atom i, then up to three reference atoms j, k, l, each followed by an internal coordinate. They can combine distances, angles and torsions in four ways:

Form

Meaning

Z_i j r_ij  k a_ijk  l b_ijkl

distance, angle, torsion

Z_i j r_ij  k a_ijk -l a_ijl

distance and two angles

Z_i j r_ij -k r_ik   l b_ijkl

two distances and torsion

Z_i j r_ij -k r_ik  -l r_il

three distances

Distances are in Å (bohr with unit=b), and angles and torsions are in degrees. In a pure Z-matrix the first atom gives only its atomic number, the second only a distance, and the third two internal coordinates. The two formats can be mixed: put the Cartesian atoms first, then the remaining atoms as a Z-matrix.

The program does not use or impose point-group symmetry unless the newer sym= option is given. Users report that ghost atoms (basis functions without a nuclear charge), which counterpoise (BSSE) corrections need, are not available. In version 25, atoms with Z=0 are accepted but carry no basis functions, so they are not ghost atoms. NICS probe points go in $nmr points= instead. Some tasks (transit, saddle, path, uniq) read several $molecule blocks from one input. Text after $end, such as the Energy = … lines that helper scripts append, is ignored. The line molecule input: '' near the top of every output is normal and not an error.

charge¶

Type: integer
Default: 0
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; Dft.rtf (default); 08 t29

Molecular charge.

mult¶

Type: integer
Default: 1
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; Dft.rtf (default); 08 t10

Spin multiplicity, 2S+1.

mass¶

Type: real
Default: none stated
Units: amu
Status: current · not verified
Sources: input.txt

Optional atomic mass for isotopes, written as mass= after an atom’s coordinates on the same atom line, in both Cartesian and Z-matrix input. Not tested in version 25.

Example:

1  0.0  0.0  0.96  mass=2.014

set¶

Type: string
Default: none stated
Status: current · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: input.txt; 03 §5 (default set); 01 §4.11, §6.2; 06 §1; 08 t01 (set=L1), t70a (set=L2)

Default: the set named by default= in the basis-file header (L1 in basis.in).

Basis set for the atoms that follow. The name must match one in the basis-set file. It can appear several times in the group. The orbital basis is paired with its own auxiliary (fitting) basis, so you cannot combine arbitrary orbital and auxiliary sets.

Example:

$molecule
 z-matrix
 set=L2
   8
 set=L1
   1    1    0.96252725
   1    1    0.96252725    2    102.943872
$end

See also: basis ($control)

unit¶

Type: string
Default: none stated
Status: undocumented · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: 01 §4.7; 08 t47

Length unit of the coordinates. The default unit is Å. In version 25, water given in bohr with unit=b gave the same geometry and energy as in Å.

Value

Meaning

b

Coordinates in bohr.

sym¶

Type: list
Default: none stated
Status: undocumented · verified on 25 (2025.02.28)
Sources: 01 §4.7; 04 #481; 08 t15; 08 t30a

Used as sym=1,0.01 in the official 2023–2025 example inputs, apparently to enable symmetry with tolerance 0.01. Newer versions report the detected point group (symmetry: D6h). In version 25, sym=1,0.01 on a slightly distorted NH3 printed symmetry: C3v    6, unique:    2 and echoed the geometry symmetrized. On its own it does not keep the symmetry during an optimization; add $optimize sym=1 for that.

See also: symmetry ($optimize)
